models.inverse_notes: A1=P*(i-g)/(1-((1+g)/(1+i))**n) needs i>g, g>=0, n>=1; checked 7550.13*0.05/(1-(1.03/1.08)**10)=1000.0 within rounding. Substitution check at g=0 collapses exactly to the ordinary-annuity PV form. The equal-rate branch P=A*n/(1+i) is a different expression for i=g, never a guard relaxation. Solving for i, g or n needs iteration or logarithms, unsupported and untested.
limitations: The equal-rate case i=g is excluded by guard; its branch P=A*n/(1+i) is a separate source-stated expression.
Beginning-of-period growing payments need the extra (1+i) timing factor (source: multiply by (1+i)), not this expression.
Solving for the rate, growth or term needs iteration or a logarithm, unsupported by the scalar grammar.

relationship.locator: Time value of money article: Present value of a growing annuity (Where i != g: PV=A/(i-g)*[1-((1+g)/(1+i))^n]; Where i = g: PV=A*n/(1+i); first-period payment definition; due variant is the same times (1+i)).
relationship.translation_notes: Local first-payment symbol renamed A1 for clarity; algebra unchanged. Dimensional check: currency divided by a dimensionless rate difference, times a dimensionless bracket, stays currency. Guards i>g and g>=0 with n>=1 preserve the source unequal-rate scope and keep all divisors nonzero. Reference exponents 10 and 4 are within the tooling cap.

sources.evidence: Article prints the growing-annuity PV with the i-g denominator and the ((1+g)/(1+i))^n term for i != g, the separate branch A*n/(1+i) for i = g, defines A as the first-period payment growing by (1+g), and notes the due variant multiplies by (1+i).
